theorems.name: Schwartz One-Factor Commodity Futures Price
theorems.description: For κ > 0 and the log spot carried in its Ornstein–Uhlenbeck Wiener representation ln S_T = m_T + σ∫₀ᵀ e^{−κ(T−s)} dB_s (the solution form of the Schwartz (1997) log-price SDE d ln S = κ(θ − ln S)dt + σ dB; that this representation solves the SDE is cited, not derived here), E[S_T] = E[exp(ln S_T)] = exp(m_T + v_T/2) with m_T = vasicekSDEMean and v_T = vasicekSDEVariance, the expectation taken under the given probability measure. Read as the pricing measure, this is the Schwartz one-factor futures price F(0,T) = E^Q[S_T]; that identification of the futures price is textbook, not proved here. Proved by composing Mathlib's Gaussian MGF (mgf_gaussianReal at 1) with the derived Gaussian law of that representation (vasicekShortRate_hasLaw_gaussian).

code.lean:
import MathFin.Models.Forwards.SchwartzOneFactor

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory Real MathFin
open scoped NNReal
open WienerIntegralL2

variable {Ω : Type*} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {μ : Measure Ω} [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
  {B : ℝ≥0 → Ω → ℝ}

/-- Schwartz one-factor futures price equals the expected terminal spot. -/
theorem schwartz_futures_price_eq_expected_spot
    (hB : IsPreBrownianReal B μ) (x₀ θ σ : ℝ) {κ : ℝ} (hκ : 0 < κ) (T : ℝ≥0) :
    ∫ ω, Real.exp (vasicekSDEMean x₀ θ κ (T : ℝ)
        + σ * (wienerIntegralLp B hB T (vasicekKernelLp κ hκ.le T) ω)) ∂μ
      = schwartzFuturesPrice x₀ θ κ σ T :=
  MathFin.schwartzFuturesPrice_eq_integral hB x₀ θ σ hκ T

metadata.reference: Schwartz (1997), 'The Stochastic Behavior of Commodity Prices: Implications for Valuation and Hedging,' Journal of Finance
metadata.formalization_scope: Full formal proof, for the constant-parameter Schwartz (1997) model with κ > 0, that E[exp(ln S_T)] = exp(m_T + v_T/2) for the log spot in its Wiener representation, under an arbitrary probability measure read as the pricing measure; that the futures price equals E^Q[S_T] is the textbook identification, not proved. Hull's time-dependent level q(t) (the Hull-White-form drift calibrated to the quoted futures curve) is out of scope. The log spot is carried in its Wiener representation (the OU solution representation of vasicekShortRate_hasLaw_gaussian) -- that this representation solves the SDE is cited, not proven here (mf-vasicek-sde-terminal-gaussian rests on the same representation). Lives in MathFin/Models/Forwards/SchwartzOneFactor.lean. Axioms-clean.

theorems.name: One OU Step Is an AR(1) Step: Gaussian Residual and σ² Recovery
theorems.description: For the Vasicek (OU) short rate with speed k > 0, one step Δt from a deterministic start r₀ (rate in its Wiener representation) has AR(1) residual ε = (r_Δt − θ) − e^{−kΔt}(r₀ − θ) distributed N(0, σ²(1 − e^{−2kΔt})/(2k)), and for Δt > 0 the calibration formula σ² = 2k·Var(ε)/(1 − e^{−2kΔt}) applied to that residual's variance returns σ². The multi-step AR(1) statement with independent innovations along a path is not formalized.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Models.Forwards.AR1OUCalibration

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory
open scoped NNReal
open MathFin

/-- **One OU step is an AR(1) step.** The residual `(r_Δt − θ) − φ·(r₀ − θ)`, `φ = e^{−kΔt}`, is
`N(0, vasicekSDEVariance σ k Δt)`, and `ouSigmaSqFromVar` applied to its variance returns `σ²`
for `Δt > 0`. Re-exports `MathFin.ouStepResidual_hasLaw` and
`MathFin.ouSigmaSqFromVar_variance_ouStepResidual`. -/
theorem ou_one_step_is_ar1
    {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] {μ : Measure Ω} [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
    {B : ℝ≥0 → Ω → ℝ} (hB : IsPreBrownianReal B μ) (r₀ θ σ : ℝ) {k : ℝ} (hk : 0 < k)
    {Δt : ℝ≥0} (hΔt : 0 < (Δt : ℝ)) :
    HasLaw (ouStepResidual hB r₀ θ σ hk Δt)
        (gaussianReal 0 (vasicekSDEVariance σ k Δt).toNNReal) μ ∧
      ouSigmaSqFromVar k (Var[ouStepResidual hB r₀ θ σ hk Δt; μ]) Δt = σ ^ 2 :=
  ⟨ouStepResidual_hasLaw hB r₀ θ σ hk Δt,
    ouSigmaSqFromVar_variance_ouStepResidual hB r₀ θ σ hk hΔt⟩

metadata.reference: P. Glasserman, Monte Carlo Methods in Financial Engineering (Springer, 2003), §3.3 (Gaussian short-rate models: the exact one-step transition of the Vasicek short rate)
metadata.formalization_scope: Full formal proof. Re-export of MathFin.ouStepResidual_hasLaw and MathFin.ouSigmaSqFromVar_variance_ouStepResidual (MathFin/Models/Forwards/AR1OUCalibration.lean), from MathFin.vasicekShortRate_hasLaw_gaussian (MathFin/Models/Rates/VasicekSDEGaussian.lean) and MathFin.ouSigmaSqFromVar_vasicekSDEVariance. SCOPE: one step from a deterministic start, the rate in its Wiener representation (its SDE cited, not proved); the multi-step AR(1) with independent innovations needs the OU Markov transition law and is not formalized; no estimator is analysed.

theorems.name: Commodity Forward with Storage Cost and Convenience Yield from No-Arbitrage
theorems.description: In a finite-state market with state prices q, discount factor DF = Σq ≠ 0 and terminal commodity prices S_T, suppose the stored commodity is priced at the spot S₀ as the claim on S_T − C + Y (storage cost C and convenience yield Y, both deterministic and paid at delivery). Then a forward with strike F has zero value exactly when F = S₀/DF + C − Y. Derived from the library's no-arbitrage forward applied to the stored-commodity claim.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Models.Forwards.TheoryOfStorage

open MathFin

/-- **Cost of carry with storage cost and convenience yield, from no-arbitrage.** If the stored
commodity is priced at `S₀` as the claim on `S_T − C + Y` and `Σ q = DF ≠ 0`, the forward at
strike `F` has zero value iff `F = S₀/DF + C − Y`. Re-exports
`MathFin.storageForward_from_no_arbitrage`. -/
theorem storage_forward_convenience_yield {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι) (q S : ι → ℝ)
    (DF S₀ C Y F : ℝ) (hDF : DF ≠ 0) (h_bond : ∑ i ∈ s, q i = DF)
    (h_carry : ∑ i ∈ s, q i * (S i - C + Y) = S₀) :
    (∑ i ∈ s, q i * (S i - F) = 0) ↔ F = S₀ / DF + C - Y :=
  storageForward_from_no_arbitrage s q S DF S₀ C Y F hDF h_bond h_carry

metadata.reference: J. C. Hull, Options, Futures, and Other Derivatives (10th ed., Pearson, 2018), ch. 5 (commodity futures: storage costs and convenience yields); H. Working, The Theory of Price of Storage, American Economic Review 39 (1949), 1254–1262
metadata.formalization_scope: Full formal proof. Re-export of MathFin.storageForward_from_no_arbitrage (MathFin/Models/Forwards/TheoryOfStorage.lean), from MathFin.forward_price_from_no_arbitrage (MathFin/Pricing/NoArbitrageDerivations.lean) applied to the claim S_T − C + Y. SCOPE: finite state space; storage cost and convenience yield are deterministic amounts paid at delivery (a proportional or stochastic convenience yield is not covered); the pricing of the stored commodity at S₀ is a hypothesis.

theorems.name: Theory-of-Storage Forward Is Sbar + C at Every Availability
theorems.description: In the canonical theory-of-storage model the spot price at availability A is S(A) = max(Sbar, f⁻¹(A)) and the convenience yield is Y(A) = max(f⁻¹(A) − Sbar, 0). With zero rates (state prices summing to 1) and the stored commodity priced at S(A) as the claim on S_T − C + Y(A), the forward with zero value has strike F = Sbar + C at every availability A: the convenience yield offsets exactly the spot's premium over the floor Sbar. The inverse demand-for-storage curve f⁻¹ is arbitrary; no monotonicity is assumed.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Models.Forwards.TheoryOfStorage

open MathFin

/-- **The storage forward does not see availability.** With `Σ q = 1`, spot `S(A)` and
convenience yield `Y(A)`, the zero-value forward strike is `Sbar + C` for every `A`.
Re-exports `MathFin.storageForward_at_availability`. -/
theorem storage_forward_kink_invariant {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι) (q S : ι → ℝ)
    (Sbar C F : ℝ) (invDemand : ℝ → ℝ) (A : ℝ) (h_bond : ∑ i ∈ s, q i = 1)
    (h_carry : ∑ i ∈ s, q i * (S i - C + convenienceYield Sbar invDemand A)
      = storageSpotPrice Sbar invDemand A) :
    (∑ i ∈ s, q i * (S i - F) = 0) ↔ F = Sbar + C :=
  storageForward_at_availability s q S Sbar C F invDemand A h_bond h_carry

metadata.reference: N. Kaldor, Speculation and Economic Stability, Review of Economic Studies 7 (1939), 1–27; H. Working, The Theory of Price of Storage, American Economic Review 39 (1949), 1254–1262
metadata.formalization_scope: Full formal proof. Re-export of MathFin.storageForward_at_availability (MathFin/Models/Forwards/TheoryOfStorage.lean): MathFin.storageForward_from_no_arbitrage at DF = 1 with the kink identity Y(A) = S(A) − Sbar (convenienceYield_eq_storageSpotPrice_sub). SCOPE: finite state space, zero rates, deterministic storage cost and convenience yield paid at delivery; the pricing of the stored commodity at S(A) is a hypothesis.

theorems.name: Sraffa's Own Rate Recovered from the No-Arbitrage Forward
theorems.description: In a finite-state market with discount factor (1 + m)^{−T} (money rate m > −1, maturity T ≠ 0) and a commodity whose loan in kind earns the own rate b > −1 (the claim on (1 + b)^T units at T is priced at the spot S₀ > 0), the forward F with zero value satisfies Sraffa's formula ((1 + m)^T·S₀/F)^{1/T} − 1 = b: the formula returns the own rate. The forward is derived from the library's no-arbitrage forward, which gives (1 + b)^T·F = S₀·(1 + m)^T.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Models.Forwards.FisherSraffaOwnRate

open MathFin

/-- **Sraffa's formula returns the own rate of the no-arbitrage forward.** With
`Σ q = (1 + m)^{−T}` and the in-kind loan priced at `S₀`, the zero-value forward `F` satisfies
`sraffaOwnRate m S₀ F T = b`. Re-exports `MathFin.sraffaOwnRate_eq_of_no_arbitrage`. -/
theorem sraffa_own_rate_from_forward {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι) (q S : ι → ℝ)
    (m b S₀ F T : ℝ) (hm : 0 < 1 + m) (hb : 0 < 1 + b) (hT : T ≠ 0) (hS₀ : 0 < S₀)
    (h_bond : ∑ i ∈ s, q i = (1 + m) ^ (-T))
    (h_own : ∑ i ∈ s, q i * ((1 + b) ^ T * S i) = S₀)
    (h_fwd : ∑ i ∈ s, q i * (S i - F) = 0) :
    sraffaOwnRate m S₀ F T = b :=
  sraffaOwnRate_eq_of_no_arbitrage s q S m b S₀ F T hm hb hT hS₀ h_bond h_own h_fwd

metadata.reference: P. Sraffa, Dr. Hayek on Money and Capital, Economic Journal 42(165) (1932), 42–53; J. M. Keynes, The General Theory of Employment, Interest and Money (1936), ch. 17
metadata.formalization_scope: Full formal proof. Re-export of MathFin.sraffaOwnRate_eq_of_no_arbitrage (MathFin/Models/Forwards/FisherSraffaOwnRate.lean), from MathFin.forward_price_from_no_arbitrage (MathFin/Pricing/NoArbitrageDerivations.lean) applied to the in-kind claim (1 + b)^T·S_T. SCOPE: finite state space; compounding by real powers (1 + m)^T and (1 + b)^T with m, b > −1 and T ≠ 0; the pricing of the in-kind loan at S₀ is a hypothesis.

theorems.name: Contango, Backwardation and Basis Convergence of the Cost-of-Carry Forward
theorems.description: For the cost-of-carry forward fxForward S r δ T = S·e^{(r−δ)T} (the library's covered-parity FX forward read with the commodity convenience yield δ in the foreign-rate slot; its derivation from no-arbitrage is proved in FxForwardParity.lean, not in this entry, which states facts about the closed form) with spot S > 0 and maturity T > 0: the forward is above the spot (contango, a normal market) exactly when the financing rate r exceeds the yield δ, below it (backwardation, an inverted market) exactly when δ exceeds r, and meets it exactly when r = δ; the maturity curve T ↦ F(T) is strictly increasing exactly when r > δ (positive net carry), strictly decreasing exactly when r < δ, and flat exactly when r = δ; and the spot-minus-forward basis S − F(T) vanishes at T = 0 and tends to 0 as T → 0⁺. The curve is the deterministic-rate forward; futures agree with it only under deterministic rates, and that identification is not proved here.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Models.Forwards.ContangoBackwardation

open MathFin Filter
open scoped Topology

/-- **The market structure of the cost-of-carry forward** `fxForward S r δ T = S·e^{(r−δ)T}`
with spot `S > 0`: contango iff `δ < r`, backwardation iff `r < δ`, the forward meets the
spot iff `r = δ`, at every maturity `T > 0`; strictly increasing iff `δ < r`, strictly decreasing iff
`r < δ`, flat iff `r = δ`; basis `S − F(T)` zero at `T = 0`, tending to `0` as `T → 0⁺`.
Bundles the eight theorems of `MathFin/Models/Forwards/ContangoBackwardation.lean`. -/
theorem contango_backwardation_basis_cluster (S r δ : ℝ) (hS : 0 < S) :
    (∀ T : ℝ, 0 < T → (S < fxForward S r δ T ↔ δ < r) ∧ (fxForward S r δ T < S ↔ r < δ) ∧
      (fxForward S r δ T = S ↔ r = δ)) ∧ (StrictMono (fxForward S r δ) ↔ δ < r) ∧
    (StrictAnti (fxForward S r δ) ↔ r < δ) ∧ ((∀ T : ℝ, fxForward S r δ T = S) ↔ r = δ) ∧
    Tendsto (fun T : ℝ ↦ S - fxForward S r δ T) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 0) ∧
    S - fxForward S r δ 0 = 0 :=
  ⟨fun T hT ↦ ⟨fxForward_contango_iff S r δ T hS hT, fxForward_backwardation_iff S r δ T hS hT,
     fxForward_eq_spot_iff S r δ T hS hT⟩, fxForward_strictMono_iff S r δ hS,
   fxForward_strictAnti_iff S r δ hS, fxForward_const_iff S r δ hS,
   fxForward_basis_tendsto_zero S r δ, fxForward_basis_zero S r δ⟩

metadata.reference: J. C. Hull, Options, Futures, and Other Derivatives (11th ed.), ch. 5 (cost of carry: the convenience yield y on a consumption asset is defined so that F₀ = S₀e^{(c−y)T}) and ch. 3 (basis defined as the spot price minus the futures price); ch. 18 (normal and inverted markets); N. Kaldor, Speculation and economic stability, Review of Economic Studies 7 (1939) 1–27; H. Working, The theory of price of storage, American Economic Review 39 (1949) 1254–1262
metadata.formalization_scope: Full formal proof of the sign, term-structure and convergence facts about MathFin.fxForward (MathFin/Models/Forwards/FxForwardParity.lean), proved in MathFin/Models/Forwards/ContangoBackwardation.lean. SCOPE: the forward is the deterministic cost-of-carry closed form S·e^{(r−δ)T} with the convenience yield δ read into the foreign-rate slot, and Hull's cost of carry c read as the financing rate alone (zero storage cost; a storage rate would add to it); volatility does not enter a forward, and the qualitative facts hold for that curve. Hull ch. 18's normal/inverted market terminology is stated there for futures prices; its application to this forward curve, and the identification of the two under deterministic rates, is not proved. The basis sign is b(T) = S − F(T), spot minus forward (Hull ch. 3's convention); TheoryOfStorage.lean's carry identity writes the same gap with the opposite sign. Normal backwardation (futures below the expected spot under the physical measure) is a different statement and is not proved.

theorems.name: Schwartz-Smith Two-Factor Commodity Model
theorems.description: For the Schwartz-Smith two-factor model, with the short-term deviation carried as the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck Wiener integral against the Vasicek kernel (chi_0*e^(-kappa*t) + sigma_chi * integral_0^t e^(-kappa*(t-s)) dB_s, the kernel-form projection of the one-factor Schwartz law), and the equilibrium level xi_t = xi_0 + nu*t + rho*sigma_xi*B1_t + sqrt(1-rho^2)*sigma_xi*B2_t for two independent pre-Brownian motions B1, B2, with ln S_t = chi_t + xi_t, rho^2 <= 1 and kappa > 0: the kernel-form projection is Gaussian N(chi_0*e^(-kappa*t), vasicekSDEVariance); the log spot is Gaussian with mean chi_0*e^(-kappa*t) + xi_0 + nu*t and total variance v_t = sigma_chi^2*(1-e^(-2*kappa*t))/(2*kappa) + 2*rho*sigma_chi*sigma_xi*(1-e^(-kappa*t))/kappa + sigma_xi^2*t (Binkowski et al. 2021 eq. (2) at gamma = 0); cov(chi_t, xi_t) = rho*sigma_chi*sigma_xi*(1-e^(-kappa*t))/kappa; ln E[S_t] = E[ln S_t] + v_t/2 (their eq. (3)); and E[S_T] equals the futures-price closed form exp(chi_0*e^(-kappa*T) + xi_0 + nu*T + v_T/2) at zero interest rate, the law-shape statement. The expectation is taken under an arbitrary probability measure read as the pricing measure; the futures-price identification is textbook, not proved.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Models.Forwards.SchwartzSmith

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory Real MathFin
open scoped NNReal
open WienerIntegralL2

variable {Ω : Type*} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {μ : Measure Ω} [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
  {B₁ B₂ : ℝ≥0 → Ω → ℝ}

/-- Schwartz-Smith log-spot law, covariance and expected spot; the deviation is the OU
integral `HullWhite.integratedRate` at zero forcing, in Wiener representation against the
Vasicek kernel — the one-factor Schwartz law is the kernel-form projection of the model. -/
theorem schwartz_smith_log_spot_law
    (hB₁ : IsPreBrownianReal B₁ μ) (hB₂ : IsPreBrownianReal B₂ μ)
    (h₁m : ∀ s, Measurable (B₁ s)) (h₂m : ∀ s, Measurable (B₂ s))
    (hind : IndepFun (fun ω s ↦ B₁ s ω) (fun ω s ↦ B₂ s ω) μ)
    {κ σ₁ σ₂ x₀ ξ₀ ν ρ : ℝ} (hκ : 0 < κ) (hρ : ρ ^ 2 ≤ 1) (t : ℝ≥0) :
    HasLaw (fun ω ↦ x₀ * Real.exp (-(κ * (t : ℝ)))
        + σ₁ * wienerIntegralLp B₁ hB₁ t (vasicekKernelLp κ hκ.le t) ω)
      (gaussianReal (x₀ * Real.exp (-(κ * (t : ℝ))))
        (vasicekSDEVariance σ₁ κ (t : ℝ)).toNNReal) μ ∧
    HasLaw (schwartzSmithLogSpot hB₁ hB₂ κ σ₁ x₀ ξ₀ ν ρ σ₂ hκ t)
      (gaussianReal (x₀ * Real.exp (-(κ * (t : ℝ))) + (ξ₀ + ν * (t : ℝ)))
        ((vasicekSDEVariance σ₁ κ (t : ℝ)
            + 2 * (ρ * σ₁ * σ₂ * (1 - Real.exp (-(κ * (t : ℝ)))) / κ)
            + σ₂ ^ 2 * (t : ℝ)).toNNReal)) μ ∧
    cov[schwartzSmithChi hB₁ κ σ₁ x₀ hκ t, schwartzSmithXi hB₁ hB₂ ξ₀ ν ρ σ₂ t; μ]
      = ρ * σ₁ * σ₂ * (1 - Real.exp (-(κ * (t : ℝ)))) / κ ∧
    ∫ ω, Real.exp (schwartzSmithLogSpot hB₁ hB₂ κ σ₁ x₀ ξ₀ ν ρ σ₂ hκ t ω) ∂μ
      = Real.exp (x₀ * Real.exp (-(κ * (t : ℝ))) + (ξ₀ + ν * (t : ℝ))
        + schwartzSmithTotalVariance κ σ₁ σ₂ ρ t / 2) := by
  refine ⟨?_, schwartzSmithLogSpot_hasLaw hB₁ hB₂ h₁m h₂m hind hκ hρ t,
    schwartzSmithChiXi_covariance hB₁ hB₂ h₁m h₂m hind hκ hρ t,
    schwartzSmithExpectedSpot hB₁ hB₂ h₁m h₂m hind hκ hρ t⟩
  have hk : HasLaw
      (fun ω ↦ σ₁ * wienerIntegralLp B₁ hB₁ t (vasicekKernelLp κ hκ.le t) ω)
      (gaussianReal 0 (vasicekSDEVariance σ₁ κ (t : ℝ)).toNNReal) μ := by
    simpa [vasicekSDEMean] using vasicekShortRate_hasLaw_gaussian hB₁ 0 0 σ₁ hκ t
  have hshift := gaussianReal_const_add (μ := 0) hk
      (x₀ * Real.exp (-(κ * (t : ℝ))))
  rw [show (0 : ℝ) + x₀ * Real.exp (-(κ * (t : ℝ)))
      = x₀ * Real.exp (-(κ * (t : ℝ))) from by ring] at hshift
  exact hshift

metadata.reference: Schwartz and Smith (2000), 'Short-Term Derivatives and Long-Term Fundamentals and Their Applications in Commodity Markets,' Management Science 46(7)
metadata.formalization_scope: Full formal proof, for the constant-parameter Schwartz-Smith model with kappa > 0, rho^2 <= 1, of: the kernel-form projection law (the one-factor Schwartz log-spot law N(chi_0*e^(-kappa*t), vasicekSDEVariance)); the Gaussian law of ln S_t (mean and total variance, Binkowski et al. 2021 eq. (2) at gamma = 0); the factor covariance (eq. 3b); ln E[S_t] (eq. 6); and the futures-price closed form E[S_T] = exp(chi_0*e^(-kappa*T) + xi_0 + nu*T + v_T/2) at zero interest rate (eq. 9's law shape). Both factors are carried in their Wiener representations against two independent pre-Brownian motions; the correlation rho enters through the shared driver B1. The long-run intercept limit and the Gibson-Schwartz convenience-yield drift reading (eqs. 12-13) are proved in the module but not restated in this snippet; the option on the futures (eq. 15) and the stochastic-convenience-yield Gibson-Schwartz SDE system are out of scope; that E[S_T] is the quoted futures price is the textbook zero-cost-of-carry identification, not proved. Lives in MathFin/Models/Forwards/SchwartzSmith.lean. Axioms-clean.
